unmapped_findings: Measured chemical composition of the Al-6 (Fe30Mn6Al1C) steel: C 0.99, Mn 29.48, Al 5.98, Fe Bal. (mass%), and measured density 7.12 g/cm³ (Table 1), the highest density/lowest Al member of the Fe30Mn(x)Al1C series.
For Al-6, the maximum true stress just before necking (σ_TS) is 1410 MPa and the fracture strength (σ_FS) is 2113 MPa (Table 2).
In addition to the Table 3 value of 34.2 ± 1.1 μm, the text separately reports an austenite grain size of 33.4 μm for the 6% Al steel (not shown in Fig. 5).
The Fe1C30Mn6Al (Al-6) alloy does not contain κ-carbides, and its yield strength (433 MPa) and impact toughness (354 J) are the lowest-strength/highest-toughness endpoints of the Al-alloyed series.
Work hardening rate of the 6% Al steel shows a maximum of around 2100 MPa; the work hardening rate increases with decreasing Al content (Fig. 8(c)).
